summary.text: Melissa Bean is the Democratic nominee for the open Illinois 8th District seat, which she represented in Congress from 2005 to 2011. A former home-based business owner who served as a member of the Blue Dog and New Democrat coalitions, she lost the seat in 2010, later worked in finance and business leadership (JPMorgan Chase, Mesirow Financial), and won the March 2026 Democratic primary. According to her campaign website, she is running on housing, healthcare, energy and education costs, workforce training, and support for workers and small business owners.

paragraphs.text: Born Melissa Luburich on January 22, 1962, in Chicago, she grew up in a Serbian-American family in the Chicago suburbs.
Attended Maine East High School, earned an associate degree from Oakton Community College in 1982, and earned a bachelor's degree from Roosevelt University in 2000.
Before elected office, was president of a home-based business, Sales Resources Inc.

Ran for the 8th District seat in 2002, losing to Republican incumbent Phil Crane with 43 percent of the vote, and defeated Crane in a 2004 rematch with 52 percent. When she took office on January 3, 2005, she became the first Democrat to represent the district since it was formed in 1935.

Served in the U.S. House from 2005 to 2011 as a member of the Blue Dog Coalition and the New Democrat Coalition, with seats on the Financial Services and Small Business committees. She lost her 2010 re-election bid to Republican Joe Walsh by 291 votes.
As a member of Congress, voted for the Affordable Care Act, TARP, the 2009 stimulus bill, the auto industry bailout, the 'Cash for Clunkers' program, and cap-and-trade climate legislation.

In 2011 became president and CEO of the Executives Club of Chicago, later served as chair of Midwest operations for JPMorgan Chase, and became CEO of Mesirow Wealth Advisors, part of Mesirow Financial, in 2019. Ballotpedia also lists affiliations with One Million Degrees, Junior Achievement and World Business Chicago.

Announced in September 2025 that she would seek her former seat after Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi entered the U.S. Senate race, and won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 31.6% of the vote in a field of eight.
Wikipedia reports she lives in unincorporated Palatine Township with her husband, Alan Bean; the page notes the residence detail needs updating.
